title: Modular Exponentiation
description: Given three integers `base`, `exp`, and `mod`, calculate `(base^exp) % mod` in O(log exp) time.
hints: Square the base modulo `mod` at each step: `base = (base * base) % mod`.
If current exponent bit is 1, multiply into result modulo `mod`.
Python's `pow(base, exp, mod)` implements binary modular exponentiation.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    base, exp, mod = int(data[0]), int(data[1]), int(data[2])
    print(pow(base, exp, mod))
